record.original_question: Let G be a finitely generated residually finite group with residual finiteness growth function F_S^G(n) = max{D(g) : |g|_S <= n}, where D(g) is the minimum index of a finite-index normal subgroup of G that does not contain the nontrivial element g. Does there exist such a group whose residual finiteness growth is intermediate, meaning that F_S^G grows faster than every polynomial function but slower than every exponential function?

evidence.quote: What is not yet well-understood is the spectrum of possible "slow" residual finiteness growth functions. For instance, the following remains open.

Question 1.3. Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group G of intermediate residual finiteness growth (that is, for which F_S^G grows faster than every polynomial but slower than any exponential function)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group with a finite symmetric generating set $S$, and let $|\cdot|_S$ denote the associated word length. Assume $G$ is residually finite, i.e., for every nontrivial $g \in G$ there is a finite-index normal subgroup of $G$ not containing $g$. For a nontrivial element $g \in G$, define
$$D(g) = \min\{[G : N] : N \trianglelefteq G,\ [G:N] < \infty,\ g \notin N\},$$
and define the residual finiteness growth function
$$F_S^G(n) = \max\{D(g) : g \in G \setminus \{e\},\ |g|_S \le n\}.$$
The asymptotic equivalence class of $F_S^G$ (up to the usual relation $f \preceq g$ iff $f(n) \le C g(Cn)$ for some constant $C > 0$) is independent of the choice of finite generating set $S$.

Question: Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group $G$ whose residual finiteness growth is intermediate, in the sense that $F_S^G(n)$ grows faster than every polynomial in $n$ and slower than every exponential function $e^{cn}$ with $c > 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly listed as open in recent problem collections on residual finiteness growth. Recent constructions (e.g., a 2025 preprint by Brieussel–Zheng–style techniques) realize a wide spectrum of residual finiteness growth functions, but only above the threshold $\exp(\varepsilon n \log n)$, leaving the intermediate (subexponential, superpolynomial) regime unresolved. Known exact asymptotics exist only for restricted classes (abelian, virtually abelian, Grigorchuk, some arithmetic groups), none of which exhibit intermediate residual finiteness growth.

status_evidence.title: A robust family of residually finite groups; spectra of residual finiteness growth
status_evidence.snippet: For any non-decreasing f with f(n) ≥ exp(εn log n) there exists a residually finite group G_f with RF_{G_f}(n) ≃ f(n).
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions realize residual finiteness growth functions only above exp(εn log n), not in the intermediate (subexponential, superpolynomial) range.

status_evidence.title: Residual finiteness growth in virtually abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Residual finiteness growth of virtually abelian groups is polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Known exact asymptotics for residual finiteness growth are confined to special classes (e.g., virtually abelian, polynomial growth).

status_evidence.title: GAGTA 2023 Problem Session
status_evidence.snippet: Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group G of intermediate residual finiteness growth?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent problem session.
